turn_text: Well, I think there's a number of things that we have to do. First and foremost, we need to put more money into research. We need to have increased research dollars. In fact, part of what came out of the hearing, which I think was a surprise to some folks, is that The impact of the human body may not be limited to folks who are drinking water with PFAS in it. There also may be a pathway through the air or even in skin contact. And certainly that's a very concerning given the fact that PFAS is put on in mental poll streets and in clothing and other ways that people may have contact with it. So certainly there's a need for additional research. The other fact that I think is absolutely critical is that the EPA has an enforceable standard. I pushed them pretty hard in that committee that we've got to have the standard. Folks need to know what is a safe level, if any, and what standards do we have to clean up to? We, I was reassured by the EPA that they thought they'd have something this fall, that they've been saying that for some time. They've always been kicking the can down the road, and we're going to keep pushing that. And I think the third area certainly is where accountability can be tied to federal properties, particularly the Department of Defense, you know, a number of military facilities where they have this type of contamination as a result of their firefighting or foam.
